description: pSIMS (parallel System for Integrating impact Models and Sectors) is a suite of tools, data and workflows that runs point-based crop models over large areas and many seasons on parallel computers, automating the preparation of weather and soil inputs and the aggregation of outputs. It was developed at the Center for Robust Decision-making on Climate and Energy Policy (RDCEP) at the University of Chicago and is described by Elliott and colleagues in a 2014 Environmental Modelling & Software paper. It drives the DSSAT (versions 4.5 and 4.6) and APSIM (7.9) crop models with gridded climate data such as AgMERRA and soils from the Harmonized World Soil Database, and writes NetCDF outputs aggregated to regions on request, at global or regional scale. The code is open source under the AGPL-3.0 licence, written with Swift parallel scripting, Python, Mono for APSIM and Java. Caveats: it targets high-performance computing clusters, depends on old model versions, and the repository shows no recent release, so it is marked stale. For simulation it produces gridded crop yield scenarios under climate change or weather shocks for food system, water and climate adaptation studies, and feeds hazard exposure analyses of farming regions. It is related to the Harmonized World Soil Database and AgERA5 records in this catalogue, which provide comparable soil and weather inputs.
